rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 reframes `timescaledb.compress` as columnstore mode on the hypertable; once columnstore is on, the engine rejects subsequent vanilla `ALTER TABLE ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. Sensor-service migration (sensor-service/src/database/migrations/1735900000000-CreateSensorMetrics.ts) audited and is unaffected — it has compression but no RLS, so no ordering conflict.

title: AddTenantCostRollup migration — TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces RLS ⊥ columnstore mutual exclusion; reorder alone insufficient
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces a HARD MUTUAL EXCLUSION between RLS and columnstore on the same hypertable. The RLS-first reorder under INFRA-CRITICAL-006 traded `operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` (compression-then-RLS) for `columnstore cannot be used on table with row security` (RLS-then-compression). Engine refuses both sequences — order does not unlock either side.
notes:
Architectural fork (must pick ONE):
  (A) keep columnstore, drop RLS — moves tenant isolation enforcement entirely to the service layer.
  (B) keep RLS, drop columnstore — preserves DB-level defense-in-depth, loses ~50% storage savings on cold buckets.

Decision: (B). User-confirmed (response: 'b'). Rationale:
- Multi-tenant SaaS — tenant isolation is the load-bearing invariant; RLS is the DB-level guard.
- Table scale at documented retention: ~29k rows/day × 90 days = ~2.6M rows total; PostgreSQL handles this trivially.
- Compression savings (~1-2 GB/year) are immaterial vs the integrity guarantee.
- Future cold-storage compression can be reintroduced via a continuous aggregate (no RLS on the aggregate, RLS-equivalent filter pushed into the materialized query) when the dataset grows enough to justify it.

Fix landed:
- Removed `ALTER TABLE … SET (timescaledb.compress, …)` block.
- Removed `add_compression_policy(…, INTERVAL '14 days', …)` call.
- Kept `create_hypertable` (for chunking) + `add_retention_policy(…, INTERVAL '90 days', …)` (for time-based pruning).
- Kept full RLS (ENABLE + FORCE + tenant_scope policy + observability_service_admin bypass).
- Down(): removed `remove_compression_policy` call (nothing to remove).
- Inline load-bearing comment documents the constraint, the architectural fork, and the chosen branch with rationale, so any future engineer attempting to add columnstore back will see the trade-off.

title: Boot signal `migration_runner_applied` never fires after db-migrate centralization — pattern only matched cold-start hot path
rule_violated: WS7 / ADR-016 Phase F deploy gate: every service in required-signals.yaml MUST emit each declared signal within its window. After db-migrate centralization, every service's migration runner sees 0 pending migrations on warm start and logs `No pending migrations on "<schema>"` — that text does NOT contain the substring `migration(s)` (with parens), so the signal never matches and the deploy gate rejects every deploy even though all containers are healthy and migrations have been applied centrally.
notes:
Architectural fix (T1, single canonical signal source):

1. MigrationRunnerService.onApplicationBootstrap() now emits a canonical end-of-run log line — `Migration runner complete for schema "<sourceSchema>": tenants=<N>` — at the success exit. Fires unconditionally on both cold-start (>0 pending applied) and warm-start (0 pending) paths. Failure paths (security throw, runner exception) intentionally do NOT emit it, so the contract still proves the runner reached the success exit (no false positive).
2. required-signals.yaml signal_library.migration_runner_applied pattern updated from `"migration(s)"` (substring of "Applied N migration(s): …") to `"Migration runner complete"` (substring of the new canonical line).
3. The pre-existing per-schema logs (`Applied N migration(s) on "X"` and `No pending migrations on "X"`) are unchanged — they still document per-schema progress; they're just no longer the contract surface for the deploy gate.
4. Refactored the orphan `if (!tenantAware) return;` early-return into a single tenantAware branch so the canonical complete log lands once per runner invocation regardless of fan-out shape.

Why not change the signal pattern alone: a looser substring like `"migration"` would match `migration failed`, `running migration`, etc. — any noise word that happens to mention migrations would falsely satisfy the contract. The canonical-log approach pins the signal to a single emission point in the code, which is the discipline required by required-signals.yaml's signalSource convention.

Both paths architectural — the tenant user path establishes the correct RLS context as soon as the tenant is discovered; the SUPER_ADMIN path uses the audit-logged bypass primitive because tenantId=NULL structurally cannot satisfy tenant_isolation_policy.
